title: Observe compiler-input namespace prefixes through owned descriptors
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds a genuine descriptor-relative namespace-classification component for the next compiler-input closure prerequisite. It replaces supplied per-path absence/object-kind facts with its own native no-follow component lookups and held O_PATH descriptors. The pre-existing owner retains raw metadata, errors and known descriptor ownership; successful diagnostic projection keeps all complete-qualification flags false.

The implementation distinguishes regular-content-unread, directory-membership-unenumerated, unresolved symlink, unsupported special object, nondirectory prefix and absence-at-pinned-parent. It does not follow intermediate or final symlinks while claiming no-follow behavior. Known descriptor ownership is consumed before one close attempt; admitted-operation/projection failures quarantine subsequent acquisition in this module. A real ENAMETOOLONG control verifies primary identity and cross-instance refusal without a private reset or replaced native primitive.

**Partial prerequisite only.** The primitive does not derive the installed compiler's effective search chain, read regular contents, resolve aliases, produce an ordinary source_files row, durably capture evidence, authenticate the original Root, or establish absolute/compilation-interval stability. The active-owner check is not a thread lock: this partial interface requires serialized nonreentrant calls and explicit protected-dispatch/noninterference premises. These are not newly accepted original compiler-input closure assumptions. Open-return ambiguity remains pending/quarantined; adverse close/delivery and original owner integration remain unqualified.

## Task and overlap

Original source investigation: [PR #6321](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6321). Frozen H25 benchmark: [PR #6029](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6029). Immediate predecessor: [PR #6354](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6354).

- Explicit user request: continue by consulting Pro, implementing and contributing upstream. This follows the completed compiler-input closure source-roots consultation and its published predecessor.
- Canonical base `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`; public head `84b0e70ba4da44b7904fe8d13903c26a3a8239e1`; exact checked tree `5c9f311a0abb0b790de0e0a192c3daeddec1e878`.
- Ten new files under `research/h25-c05-namespace-observer/`, one commit, no shared/frozen source edits or unmerged executable dependency.
- Immediate predecessor #6354 `b3771dbc5f713ba3e90170c1dc3321e653222c65` constructs fixed roots and a conditional prefix certificate over supplied lookup facts. This contribution adds actual namespace observations; it does not repeat or run that predecessor. #6352 publishes earlier bootstrap-control campaign source resolutions; #6351 clarifies original G12 scope. PR6321/6029/5864 and separate #6339/#6346/#6347 scopes/credit are retained.
- Fresh metadata for the declared 21-node lineage, all-state compiler-input closure/caller/namespace overlap searches, and the H25 hub were checked. No newer compiler-input closure implementation was found within that scope; this is not a global novelty/exhaustiveness claim. Current main/rules were refreshed before publication.
- Scope changed from the retained portable-replay card to the explicitly assigned compiler-input closure source-observation prerequisite. Full original compiler-input closure and bootstrap-control campaign are not narrowed or declared complete.
- The completed actual Pro follow-up supplied the two source files. Observer SHA256 `d52913c0e0a25457aa1fac39459321134304a15ac7788bd0115ddf3c8a2ba882` (11,960 bytes) and proposed fixture controls `ed1ddeff64acf69900e55ac00a38bdf1b6d249a6fc4e5843cd372f9b95618dd7` (6,653 bytes) are unchanged. Codex independently audited them and authored the separate control suite/runner. Pro reported AI source review, not executed validation or inspectable human acceptance.

## Validation

Executed locally on Python 3.12.3:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/h25-c05-namespace-observer --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/h25-c05-namespace-observer
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/h25-c05-namespace-observer
```

Metadata/pins, all four registered commands and the ten-file committed-byte preflight passed. Each Python profile (normal and optimized) passed the two Pro-proposed test methods and independent controls covering 18 successful observation scenarios, 14 pure input refusals, 133 closed-descriptor EBADF probes, one actual ENAMETOOLONG/quarantine control and two temporal counterexamples. The 526 internal checks per independent run are fixture checks; they do not establish complete original control families.

Fixture expectations are fixed independently before candidate observation. Controls include distinct and empty regular objects, mode-zero classification without a readability claim, final/intermediate/dangling symlinks, FIFO, PCH object alternatives, hardlink path distinction, the exact 64-component/65-descriptor positive, actual error retention and post-failure acquisition refusal. Outcome ABA demonstrates absence/presence/absence; complete metadata endpoint equality is not claimed. A separate real-OS ancestor rename demonstrates that a held directory need not remain at its old absolute spelling.

Only this new component and fresh owned temporary fixtures were executed. The suites create no subprocess and import no original Root/provider/producer/helper or archived candidate. No compiler, native extension build, historical control, target process or scientific workload was executed. Fixtures and raw local output are retained. An initial sparse-staging refusal and premature pre-commit byte-check failure are preserved locally; staging was corrected only for the new package. A validation-field wording clarification changed no tested Python bytes. No functional source repair was needed.

Exact remote branch, tree and sole canonical parent were read back. Hosted checks are pending at submission. The fixed 60-minute unit has its own source gate, 30-minute no-progress stop and hard deadline; it does not restart the old bootstrap-control campaign round. Local source bounds (at most 65 held FDs and 324 Python-level primitive invocations per supported path) are not kernel-syscall, wall-time or complete-cost bounds. Original limits (512 rows, 64 MiB/file, 256 MiB/capture) and parent fit obligations remain unchanged. Whole compiler-input closure, bootstrap controls and authentic serializer qualification, source adoption, performance and kappa credit remain open; unknown costs remain OPEN_NOT_ZERO.

Retain original source/reviewer, PR6321/6029/5864, unpaidmoon/Cursor Grok PR6339 and Douglas R. Colkitt's circuit/network/native/verification attribution. New code/analysis Apache-2.0. AI assessment and finite filesystem checks are not human or proof-kernel acceptance.

## Open next questions

Bind the installed configured toolchain's source/build rules and actual inherited caller context; derive complete search/expansion, alias/content/PCH handling and genuine original Root/writer/compilation-interval currentness integration. Prove whole-domain witness representation and complete fit/cost under unchanged limits. The smallest consequential next source step is an exact rule/context adapter for the pinned original executable; distribution correspondence is still missing. See README and TASK.json for the conditional argument, explicit unexecuted adverse cases and next dependency. No new trust premise, original execution budget or automatic prior-round restart follows from this contribution.
